thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Production alert — surge of 429s on inference-prod: /v1/generate and /v1/stream endpoints. 429 rate 12% over last 5m. paging oncall.
Alice (oncall): on it. Checking dashboard now: https://console.redwood/dashboard/ingress/429?range=15m
Alice (oncall): p95 latency unchanged ~220ms, p99 climbed from 900ms -> 1.6s, but 429s are the main problem. Appears concentrated in us-west-2.
Ben (sre): any tenant spikes? run query for per-tenant 5m error rate.
Alice (oncall): running quick aggregate... `SELECT tenant, count(*) FILTER (status=429) / count(*) AS rate FROM requests WHERE ts > now()-interval '5m' GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY rate DESC LIMIT 10;`
Alice (oncall): top offenders: acme-inc 48% of 429s (not of traffic), sandbox-qa 18%, default-unknown 9%. acme-inc traffic has lot of long sequences (streaming).
Carla (support): I've already had two ACME incidents opened by CSMs, they see user-facing errors. Not good. They're in production.
Dave (eng-runtime): streaming endpoints have tighter concurrency; wondering whether a small kernel bug is amplifying transient backpressure. But we should mitigate for customers now.
Ben (sre): immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply per-tenant soft cap for acme-inc 20 req/s 2) disable streaming for non-enterprise keys 3) enable short-circuit cache for common prompt prefixes 4) roll a global emergency throttle policy if needed.
Alice (oncall): I'm going to set per-tenant cap for acme-inc now. Command: ```
curl -X POST "https://ops.redwood/api/v1/ratelimits/apply"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"policy":"per_tenant_cap","tenant":"acme-inc","max_rps":20,"duration_s":900}'
```
Alice (oncall): applied and received 200 OK. Policy id `policy-2026-03-acme-001`.
incident-bot: Action recorded: rate limit applied (policy-2026-03-acme-001) by Alice (oncall).
Carla (support): Informing ACME CSMs: "We've applied a temporary cap to reduce error surface while we investigate. We'll follow up with timeline." @acme-ops
Ben (sre): Next, disable streaming for non-enterprise keys. Alice, can you flip `streaming.enabled = false` for tier=free and tier=dev?
Alice (oncall): doing: ```
PATCH /admin/config
{
  "scope": "global",
  "modifications": [{"key":"streaming.enabled","value":false,"filter":"tier in (free, dev)"}]
}
```
Alice (oncall): patch accepted, streaming toggled off for free/dev.
Dave (eng-runtime): toggling streaming will drop some long-lived conns; we should watch connection churn. Started a short burn-in watch on conn_count and p99 connect time.
Alice (oncall): enabling short-circuit cache for embeddings/prefix hits: `cache.set('prefix_shortcircuit', true)` via ops CLI.
Alice (oncall): done. Also enabled sampling-based early-accept for repeat prompts (10% sampling) to reduce backend load.
Ben (sre): pulling dashboard: 429 rate dropped from 12% -> 4% in 7m. P95 latency steady. Link: https://console.redwood/dashboard/ingress/429?range=30m&filters=tenant:acme-inc
Alice (oncall): good sign. But we still see elevated 503s on two worker pools in us-west-2. Investigating logs.
Dave (eng-runtime): 503s seem to be internal upstream OOM backpressure in runtime-gpu-3. I'm increasing fallback capacity to cpu-fallback pool for short tasks: `orchestrator scale --pool cpu-fallback --add 8`.
incident-bot: Orchestrator job submitted: scale cpu-fallback +8 by Dave (eng-runtime). JobID: scale-8821
Ben (sre): Also apply emergency global throttle policy if 429 > 5% across region for 10m. Alice, wanna go ahead if we slip back?
Alice (oncall): agreed. I'm going to put an automated policy in place but disabled. If 5% threshold breaches again, it will auto-toggle and notify.
Alice (oncall): created auto-trigger `global-emergency-throttle-v1` (throttle to 50rps global weighted by tier) with trigger threshold 5% 10m.
Carla (support): Notifying enterprise accounts: short note to impacted customers and recommending retries/backoff. Ticket updated for ACME, tagging follow-up for eng postmortem.
Ben (sre): Heads-up: I'm taking over in 10m for the next handoff. Alice, can you summarize actions and any remaining unknowns?
Alice (oncall): summary: (1) per-tenant cap applied to acme-inc (policy-2026-03-acme-001), (2) streaming disabled for free/dev, (3) short-circuit cache + early-accept enabled, (4) cpu-fallback pool scaled +8, (5) auto-trigger created but not active. Unknowns: root cause for acme-inc pattern (prompt shape?), runtime OOM behavior in gpu-3 pool. Logs and heap dumps collected.
Ben (sre): I'll monitor next 30m, if stable we'll remove per-tenant cap gradually and re-enable streaming for dev later. Also will schedule heapdump analysis with runtime team.
Alice (oncall): handing off now. Ben is primary. I'm going offline for scheduled family thing. :wave:
Ben (sre): acknowledged. Taking over — will post updates. If 429 rate breaches 6% again I'll enable auto-trigger. ping @carla for support comms.
incident-bot: ALERT: Mitigation in progress. Current 429 rate 3.8% (5m). Next automated check in 2m. Logs and actions documented in incident channel thread: /incidents/1769600000
Carla (support): I'll keep ACME and other flagged customers updated. Opening a post-incident ticket for root cause and customer impact tally.
Dave (eng-runtime): copying runtime team and creating issue: `ENGRT-5321` for gpu-3 OOM investigation. Attaching heap dumps.
Ben (sre): thanks team. Will update in-thread with any changes. If anyone sees regression, tag @ben (sre) and escalate to paging.
